protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; property-pins-only entry
summary: Seven of the eight axes come back clean, and the entry's structural discipline is good: it authorizes the MF-6 rewrite without performing it, refuses to bundle DESIGN-READY, coins no status token, smuggles no SATISFIED, leaves condition 5 untouched, does not amend D-001, and pins COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md at the current 7c6d8a56. It also does something better than most entries in this lineage — clause 3 predicts and names the one lawful re-open its own execution will cause, rather than discovering it later. One MUST-FIX. The freeze §7.10 section digest in the measured-inputs table does not reproduce. I could not derive it from the section under eight normalizations, a bounded probe over twenty candidate start lines and spans up to two hundred lines, two heading-to-next-heading readings, or a whole-file sweep across the freeze and every artifact in the corpus. That matters more here than it would elsewhere, because D-033 is the entry that establishes section pinning as the corpus's citation form, and its own section pin is the one that does not resolve.

objections.claim: The freeze §7.10 section digest is unreproducible, and the entry states no extraction rule by which a later reader could derive it.
objections.evidence: The measured-inputs table reads: freeze e809d4395f394a507c36c23c069d566c838b2283c931b6d2d13797be53406dbd (§7.10 section 2416e1e5170ca05633fdb277e5bc7117ba683d99db566ff5b4fd785de877b4e4). The whole-file freeze digest is correct — I re-measured it. The section digest is not. Section §7.10 begins at line 4449, 'Structural: a guard that pins a decision's CURRENT state asserts that state will never change', and the next heading of any level is '## 8. Implementer litmus' at line 4610, so the section is lines 4449 through 4609. I tested that range under eight normalizations: newline-joined with and without a trailing newline, with and without the heading line, with per-line trailing whitespace stripped, with blank lines removed, CRLF-joined, and whole-text stripped. The results were 8dd44398, 7bfa72c4, 84611a21, 5222cb9a, 8dd44398, 5d03b771, 0325eb4d and 9f52425e. None is the claimed digest. I then ran a bounded probe: every contiguous line range beginning at any of lines 4441 through 4460 and running up to two hundred lines, hashed with and without a trailing newline. No match. I also swept every whole file — the freeze itself and every .json and .md in docs/coop/artifacts — and the digest is not any of them. So the claimed value is not the section under any reading I could construct, and the entry supplies no rule that would fix the reading. This is the same defect class I raised at IR-HEA3-A1 against host-effect-authorization.v3, where a section pin carried no extraction rule and the natural reading produced a different digest; that artifact repaired it by stating the rule in terms of delimiters and recording the non-matching alternative explicitly. D-033 needs the same treatment, and needs it more, because this is the entry that makes section pinning the corpus's practice — clause 1 converts DR-001 and five other rows' citations to '(path, named section or selector, segment hash)'. An entry that establishes a citation form should carry an instance of that form which resolves.
objections.proposedFix: Recompute the §7.10 segment hash over a stated range and record the rule that produces it, in the form the HEA lineage settled on: name the delimiters, give the line range as a convenience only, and record at least one non-matching alternative so the wrong reading cannot recur. If the intended subject was not the whole of §7.10 but a narrower passage — for example the single sentence clause 1 relies on — say which passage and pin that.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: b4cd79192ea43ad988fbc41e29f456f8fd54d09160123a62450e964d4534cdd2 both times. No drift.

The COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md pin is current, which the review prompt flags specifically: the table reads 7c6d8a568ee58c4a1b27a2a4a40005dd83f85b40f75011677554d9d1f95805e6 and I re-measured that exact value. Not stale.

The freeze whole-file pin is correct at e809d4395f394a507c36c23c069d566c838b2283c931b6d2d13797be53406dbd, and file 08 at 877e36d3b597fb9b51c1c91fb6b6c6f27eabdcb8b2b1a941ade2b34850a0f58f. Only the section digest fails.

The property the entry relies on is real even though its digest is not derivable. Freeze line 4449 reads '### 7.10 Structural: a guard that pins a decision's CURRENT state asserts that state will never change', which is exactly the rule the decision-type line paraphrases as 'pin the property, not the current value'. So the finding is a citation defect, not a false premise.

No silent D-001 amendment. The decision-type line states 'Does not amend D-001's five conditions'; clause 3 preserves the D-001 two-stage DR-001 route by name, 'regeneration MEASURED now; SATISFIED only after DR-204 audits the disposition'; clause 5 leaves condition 5 unchanged. Nothing in the entry restates, narrows or quotes the five conditions.

No new file-08 status token. Clause 4 states the vocabulary stays closed and cites D-006 turn-2 NOTE-03, which I verified exists in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md. Sweeping the draft for register status tokens returns DESIGN-READY twice, IMPLEMENTED once and QUALIFIED once — all inside the 'Not in this entry' exclusion block and the Alternatives rejection, none coined or applied.

The MF-6 rewrite is not performed here. Clause 2 states 'This entry authorizes that rewrite. It does not perform it. Performing it is a file-08 content change and needs its own D-000-reviewed commit (D-001 MF-6)', and Alternatives rejects 'Perform the file-08 rewrite in this same commit. Rejected: MF-6.'

DESIGN-READY is not bundled. The header block excludes live-register-versus-history presentation, the three assurance stages, and any amendment of condition 5, and Alternatives rejects the combined form as bundling while naming it reachable later.

No SATISFIED smuggled. The token occurs three times and every occurrence is negative or descriptive: clause 3's 'The SATISFIED re-record remains the D-001 two-stage act' and 'SATISFIED only after DR-204 audits the disposition', and the readiness effect's 'Zero SATISFIED'.
Condition 5 is not authorized. Clause 5 states it is unchanged, and no clause mentions docs/v2/implementation/.

A property I checked because entries in this lineage have got it wrong: clause 3 predicts the consequence of its own execution rather than leaving it to be discovered. 'Executing clause 2 will re-open DR-001 by today's scope clause. That re-open is expected.' Given that DR-001's recorded history is a treadmill of re-opens, an entry that authorizes a scope-clause rewrite and does not say the rewrite itself trips the old clause would have been defective. This one says it.

The reversibility class carries a temporal boundary matched to its own dependent: 'total before the MF-6 rewrite lands. After that rewrite, overturn also requires reverting or superseding the rewrite commit.' That is the construction the D-025-031 cycle settled on and it is used correctly here.

D-000 clause 3 completeness, field by field: id, date, title, status, decision, alternatives (three, each with a reason), rationale carried by the decision-type basis line, decision type, reversibility class, overturn procedure, readiness effect. Reviewer verdict and commit land at adoption.

convergenceNote: Turn 1 of 3, one MUST-FIX, and it is mechanical rather than substantive. I contest nothing D-033 decides: the citation-form conversion, the refusal to perform the rewrite here, the refusal to bundle, the closed status vocabulary, the untouched condition 5, and the predicted single re-open all survive attack. The repair is to recompute one segment hash and state the rule that derives it, in the form this corpus already settled on in the host-effect lineage. I recorded two of the candidate digests I measured so that whichever range is intended, the wrong readings are on the record and cannot recur.
